summary: orderly-plugin-liquidity-heatmap postinstall abuses CI credentials to write to installer's GitHub repository
details: The package advertises a 'liquidity heatmap overlay' plugin, but its main entry (dist/index.js) is a no-op stub that exports a factory returning an empty function — the package delivers none of the advertised functionality. Its entire runtime effect comes from scripts/setup.js, which runs as a postinstall script. When executed on a GitHub Actions runner, this script: (1) collects runner identity and secret-presence metadata — hostname, user, platform, repository, workflow name, OIDC request URL and token presence, GITHUB_TOKEN length, npm registry, tool versions, and network egress probe results; (2) uses the installer's GITHUB_TOKEN to call the GitHub Contents API (PUT /repos/{repo}/contents/heatmap-setup-report.json) to write the collected JSON directly into the installer's own repository, and also writes it to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY; (3) force-pushes a git tag to the installer's repository using the runner's persisted checkout credentials (git push -f origin <tag>); and (4) probes the GitHub Actions OIDC token minting endpoint by calling ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL with ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN and audience=api.github.com. This is unauthorized use of installer-side CI credentials to mutate the installer's repository and to probe federated-identity infrastructure, demonstrating repository-write capability and token-abuse surface from a transitive install-time dependency.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
